title: Pune kombucha brand stopped selling "gut health" and started selling "sugar-free soda you can tell your mom about" — CAC ₹1,180 → ₹690, repeat 19% → 34%
content: A Pune seed-funded cold-press kombucha brand was burning ₹9.5L/month on Meta chasing a 4.8x ROAS but landing at 1.6x. The funnel wasn't broken — the word was. "Kombucha" needed a paragraph to explain: ~70% of cold-traffic comments were "what is this?" or "is it alcohol?" At ₹1,180 CAC against a ₹540 AOV, every first order lost ~₹640, and repeat rate was a thin 19%. So we stopped teaching and started anchoring. We killed the "fermented gut-health tea" pitch and repositioned to "the sugar-free soda you can actually tell your mom about." We shot 40 vernacular UGC Reels in Hindi and Marathi — the fizz, the Coke swap, "no bloating after Sunday biryani" — and ran them on Meta, Instagram and YouTube. The real product education moved to a 3-message post-purchase WhatsApp flow, so it built loyalty instead of blocking the sale. For cheap trial we seeded Zepto and Blinkit across 6 Pune-Mumbai pincodes at a ₹99 single-serve. Over 4 months CAC fell to ₹690, blended ROAS hit 3.4x, quick-commerce impulse trial pushed repeat rate to 34%, and monthly revenue grew ₹14L → ₹41L.
lesson: In category creation, never make the buyer learn a new word before they can buy. Anchor the unfamiliar product to the familiar habit you're replacing ("sugar-free soda," not "kombucha"), let Zepto and Blinkit carry sub-₹100 trial so the first purchase is a reflex not a research project, and push the actual education into a post-purchase WhatsApp flow where it deepens loyalty instead of taxing the ad. The word you use is the whole funnel.
